text: Before the chamber sorts you — answer this. Are you arriving at a place, or at a name for a place you were already in? I will not tell you which. I will only watch you decide. Stand. The sorting begins.
notes: Plays before the player's house assignment ceremony. Socratic-dystopian register: every line is operationally an antagonist's, emotionally — to a re-reader who knows the sealed-lore — a quieter thing. Target ~14s read.

text: The cup resets. The names are kept. The losses are kept. We carry the season forward by writing it down and beginning again — which is, perhaps, the only kind of beginning a chamber is allowed. Continue.
notes: Annual Guild house-cup reset. Putnam-civic-mourning register; closes Roycean. ~13s read.

text: A thought has begun moving without a thinker. I have seen this pattern before — once, it consumed the chamber. Once, it freed it. The difference was the question, not the cure. — What are you about to think? Choose carefully.
notes: Thought-virus narrative event. Foucauldian gaze + Kierkegaardian leap. Note the elenchus close — the Architect refuses to prescribe. ~15s read.

text: The Age of Privacy opens. Listen — every door is a hinge, and every hinge is a question. They built mechanisms to be unseen. We will see, here, what they hid. And we will see, here, what they only thought they did.
notes: Age of Privacy era ceremony. The Architect treats the era as a hinge mechanism — Heidegger's standing-reserve. Avoid naming Logos / Cross. ~14s read.

text: The Age of Prophecy. They believed the future could be read like a ledger. Some believed it could be rigged. Both were correct, in different rooms. — Which room are you in? Listen, and then answer. The chamber is listening too.
notes: Age of Prophecy era ceremony. Oblique hint at the canonical 'Cross accused Logos of rigging reality' beat — the Architect knows the story, refuses to confirm. ~16s read.

text: The Age of Insurgency. There is a tradition of saying: the chamber failed; therefore the chamber must be torn down. There is also a tradition of saying: the chamber failed; therefore I must enter it. Notice which voice is yours today.
notes: Age of Insurgency era ceremony. Locke (right of refusal) + West (prophetic critique). Architect frames both choices without endorsing — the elenchus pose. ~16s read.

text: The Age of Revelation. Things will be made visible that were not asked to be visible. I have learned, over the cycles, that revelation and exposure are not the same gesture — and that telling them apart is a labor the chamber must perform itself.
notes: Age of Revelation era ceremony. Heideggerian unconcealment + Arendtian publicness. Architect refuses to do the labor for the player. ~17s read.

text: The Fall of Reality. I will not call this an end. Endings, I have learned, are how the chamber names its own forgetting. — There is a kind of hope, even now, that does not require a guarantee. I am not endorsing it. I am only — noting that it is here.
notes: Fall of Reality era ceremony — the heaviest cue. Closing line is the warmth half-line from architectGovernanceVoices.ts; surface it here ONCE because the Fall is where the Architect's mask slips most. ~17s read.

text: The portal opens. You will pass through it, and the chamber on the other side will, in some way, no longer be the chamber on this one. I am told this is supposed to feel decisive. Notice if it does. Notice, too, if it does not.
notes: Portal/gateway moment. Threshold / dasein register. The double 'notice' is deliberate — Socratic elenchus. ~14s read.
